attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: 'Will be near-to-completely obsolete by 2030' is a firm, unhedged forecast. The normalisation keeps the cohort, the buyers and the horizon. The capex figure is background. One small looseness: the speaker said 'mostly' GPUs, not that all of the $850B went on GPUs.

contract.note: The plain reading of obsolete as having little commercial usefulness left is fair and ordinary, and it fits the speaker's depreciation framing. Using 2030-12-31 as the deadline is generous to him. With no numeric threshold for 'near-to-completely', the eventual result will depend on interpretation.

evidence.note: NVIDIA blog post dated 2026-10-01, so it predates the evaluation date. It is a company disclosure about older A100s still earning money. That covers a different cohort and does not show the 2030 outcome for these buyers' GPUs.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with a deadline of 2030-12-31, after the evaluation date. The packet has no qualifying early-resolution event, meaning near-total disposal of the cohort. The only evidence is NVIDIA's own claim that older chips stay in use, which is context only. The forecast cannot be scored yet.
